summary.headline: PNC Infratech Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 34% YoY to Rs 1,518 crore and PAT to Rs 271 crore, while management kept FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 6,000 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue rose 34% YoY to Rs 1,518 crore, with EBITDA of Rs 375 crore (24.7% margin) and PAT of Rs 271 crore (17.8% margin). Consolidated revenue was Rs 1,688 crore (+19% YoY) and consolidated EBITDA Rs 524 crore (31% margin). Management kept FY27 and FY28 revenue guidance and new-business targets unchanged. The call was dominated by the Kanpur-Lucknow expressway issue, where NHAI has issued a show cause notice to the SPV and management declined to discuss the possible non-performer or bidding-ban outcome.

financial_highlights.value: Net worth Rs 6,084 crore; bank debt Rs 428 crore (D/E 0.07x excl. ICD); cash and investments Rs 1,046 crore; net cash surplus Rs 133 crore
Net worth Rs 7,147 crore; total debt Rs 5,448 crore (D/E 0.76x); cash and bank Rs 2,870 crore
About Rs 20 crore in Q1, guided run-rate about Rs 20 crore/quarter
financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs 30 crore in Q4

segments.name: Highways (EPC/HAM/BOT)
segments.commentary: Highway contracts are 64% of the Rs 19,100 crore unexecuted order book. Management says the road unexecuted order book is slightly above 60%. Fund-based portfolio is 17 projects: 1 BOT-Toll, 2 BOT-Annuity, 14 HAM.

segments.name: Water (Jal Jeevan Mission and irrigation)
segments.commentary: Opening water order book was Rs 2,310 crore; Rs 136 crore executed in Q1, leaving about Rs 2,180 crore. About Rs 741 crore (ex-GST) is due from government. Andhra Pradesh irrigation: Rs 416 crore invoiced, Rs 263 crore received, Rs 153 crore receivable.

segments.name: Coal mining
segments.commentary: Mining EPC targeted at about Rs 500 crore revenue in FY27 and similar in FY28; Q1 execution was low due to land-access problems, and two new surface miners were deployed.

segments.name: Pune Ring Road
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about Rs 75 crore. Billing is milestone-linked to precasting and erection, so it is lumpy; management did not give FY27/FY28 revenue numbers.

segments.name: Solar (MP, NHPC PSA route)
segments.commentary: EPC component about Rs 2,000 crore on more than 300 acres leased in Madhya Pradesh. Work to start in Q4 FY27; more than Rs 1,000 crore revenue targeted in FY28, balance in FY29. Equity requirement about Rs 400 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about Rs 6,000 crore and FY28 of Rs 7,500 crore, with about 12% margin, maintained unchanged.
New business target of Rs 12,000-15,000 crore for FY27 maintained; management said about Rs 5,900 crore has been secured so far.
JJM revenue targeted at Rs 700-800 crore in FY27 and about Rs 1,000 crore in FY28; project to complete by December 2028.
Andhra Pradesh irrigation: Rs 150 crore targeted in FY27, balance about Rs 600 crore in FY28, subject to timely payment.
Effective tax rate guided at 25-27% for FY27. Capex guided at about Rs 150 crore for standalone FY27 and FY28 (Q1 spend about Rs 70 crore), plus about Rs 350 crore on the mining project.
Equity: Rs 436 crore remaining for existing HAMs over two years (about Rs 226 crore in FY27); about Rs 400 crore for the two new HAMs, mainly in FY28-29.
Pantnagar airport expected before end-September 2026; Bhopal bypass AD pushed to Q3 CY26 due to scope change.
capex_capacity: Standalone capex guided at about Rs 150 crore for FY27 and about Rs 150 crore for FY28; Rs 70 crore spent on machinery in Q1.
Coal mining project total capex about Rs 350 crore (management corrected from Rs 150 crore), front-loaded in the initial years.

Two new HAM SPVs (Barabanki-Mustafabad and Mustafabad-Biswariya) signed concession agreements with NHAI on 16 July 2026; 150 days allowed for financial closure, and appointed date depends on NHAI handing over 90% of land.
HAM portfolio: 6 projects at COD/PCOD, 5 under construction, 1 (MPRDC) with financial closure documents submitted, 2 new projects in financial closure.
Rs 1,187 crore of HAM equity infused to June 2026 out of Rs 1,623 crore requirement (excluding the two new HAMs).
demand_pricing: Unexecuted order book about Rs 19,100 crore (mgmt said Rs 19,600 crore earlier in call, then Rs 19,100 crore per prepared remarks). It is 64% highways, about 21% water/canal/railway/airport, about 15% coal mining.

Bids submitted: 24 projects worth about Rs 32,000 crore (16 EPC, 8 HAM), including 10 HAM, 8 railway, 2 coalfield. A further about 78 projects (about Rs 1.7 lakh crore) are to be bid in the next 2-3 months.
NHAI's Q1 FY27 awards were 107 km and execution about 640 km; NHAI plans to bid out 54 projects worth about Rs 1.8 lakh crore over 2-3 months.
Management targets a non-road share of about 40-45% over time, versus about 60% road order book today.
Management did not comment on pricing or competition.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for Kanpur-Lucknow issue (non-performer or bidding ban), possible duration, UP-level bidding impact, repair cost and standalone vs subsidiary impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment beyond exchange filings. NHAI has issued a show cause notice to the concessionaire SPV; reply is being submitted and the decision rests with NHAI, so no timeline or ban duration was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 and FY28 guidance changing, given about Rs 5,900 crore of new business secured versus Rs 12,000-15,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: No change. FY27 revenue Rs 6,000 crore, FY28 Rs 7,500 crore, about 12% margin and FY27 new business target Rs 12,000-15,000 crore all maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Barabanki-Mustafabad appointed date and equity quantum for the two new HAMs?
qa_highlights.answer: Concession agreements signed 16 July 2026 with 150 days for financial closure. Appointed date follows NHAI handing over 90% of land. Equity expected around Rs 400 crore, not Rs 490 crore as the analyst suggested.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital details: inventory, debtors, payables, mobilisation advance, retention, unbilled and HAM/water debtors?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory Rs 847 crore, debtors Rs 1,900 crore, trade payables Rs 680 crore, mobilisation advance Rs 178 crore, retention Rs 295 crore, unbilled Rs 462 crore, HAM debtors Rs 479 crore, water debtors Rs 925 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise in Q1 and what is the ICD and interest outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose due to a term loan for machinery financing, repayable over 4-5 years. ICD is Rs 485 crore. Quarterly interest run-rate about Rs 20 crore, and debt is expected to decline.

qa_highlights.question: Water (JJM and AP irrigation) revenue targets and receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: JJM revenue Rs 700-800 crore in FY27 and about Rs 1,000 crore in FY28, project completion by December 2028. Rs 741 crore excluding GST is due from government. AP irrigation Rs 150 crore in FY27 and about Rs 600 crore in FY28, with Rs 153 crore receivable and Rs 94 crore release expected within 7-10 days.

qa_highlights.question: Coal mining and solar revenue and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Coal mining revenue about Rs 500 crore each in FY27 and FY28; total mining capex about Rs 350 crore, front-loaded. Solar EPC about Rs 2,000 crore with equity about Rs 400 crore; solar revenue minimal in FY27, more than Rs 1,000 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Order book reconciliation versus last quarter's Rs 22,000 crore figure?
qa_highlights.answer: The earlier Rs 22,000 crore included the two new HAMs; the current unexecuted order book is about Rs 19,100 crore, including the two HAMs, Pantnagar airport, Ganga bridge and LDA flyover.

risks_watch: Kanpur-Lucknow expressway: NHAI show cause notice to SPV, possible non-performer or bidding-ban outcome, toll loss and repair cost still unquantified; management gave no timeline.
Receivables: JJM Rs 741 crore excluding GST pending from government and AP irrigation receivable; working capital at 110 days depends on these collections.
NHAI award slowdown (107 km awarded in Q1) and unclear timing of the Rs 1.8 lakh crore bid pipeline; Rs 32,000 crore bids under evaluation with financial bids not yet opened.
Execution timing risks: Pune Ring Road billing is lumpy and FY27/FY28 revenue not given; coal mining Q1 execution hit by land-access issues; solar work only from Q4 FY27 pending PSA/PPA.
Two new HAMs need financial closure within 150 days and appointed date depends on NHAI handing over 90% of land; Pantnagar airport target end-September 2026 and Bhopal bypass moved to Q3 CY26.

Balance sheet: debt rose to about Rs 900 crore including Rs 485 crore ICD despite Rs 1,100 crore cash, with a new machinery term loan; management did not fully explain the rationale beyond liquidity strategy.
Order book reconciliation was confusing (Rs 22,000 crore vs Rs 19,600 crore vs Rs 19,100 crore), and some figures were corrected during the call (mining capex, equity for new HAMs).
key_quotes: So, we are maintaining the same guidance.
we don't want to share anything beyond what we informed to the exchanges.
Testing is going on, so this month everything will be clear.
So, we expect this funds will be realized in the coming months, because the state government is actively pursuing release of 50% subsidy from the Government of India.
summary.management_tone: Confident on guidance, order pipeline and margins, but guarded and evasive on the Kanpur-Lucknow NHAI matter, refusing to discuss non-performer, bidding-ban or toll-loss outcomes. Several figures were given loosely or corrected mid-call, and some answers were deferred to after the call.
